# Markdown Decisions

Documentation is read where it is rendered, so it is checked against the format its renderer reads and against the files it points to. The checks wrap the tools that own those rules and need them installed; a project without them has an incomplete analysis, never a clean one.

## Format

A Markdown file is valid GitHub Flavored Markdown.

| id | title | check | fix | requirement |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`markdown/gfm`](#markdown-follows-github-flavored-markdown) | Markdown follows GitHub Flavored Markdown | warn · command | unsafe |  |

### Markdown follows GitHub Flavored Markdown

`markdown/gfm` · file · warn · command · fix: unsafe · markdown

*A document is read rendered, and a construct the renderer reads differently from the author (a heading without its space, a list that restarts, a fence that never closes) is a defect the author does not see. markdownlint-cli2 owns these rules (MD001 to MD059) and fixes the ones it marks fixable, so the decision runs it and does not restate them. It reads the repository's own `.markdownlint-cli2.*` configuration, which is where a project turns a rule off. The program is not bundled. A project without markdownlint-cli2 on its `PATH` has an incomplete analysis for its Markdown files, and a finding is never invented in its place. The finding of a file that fails is the end of what the tool printed, which names each rule and line.*

A Markdown file MUST pass markdownlint-cli2.

Derived from: GitHub Flavored Markdown spec: https://github.github.com/gfm/; markdownlint-cli2: https://github.com/DavidAnson/markdownlint-cli2; markdownlint rules: https://github.com/DavidAnson/markdownlint/blob/main/doc/Rules.md

```diff
--- a/example.md
+++ b/example.md
@@ -3 +3 @@
-#Broken heading
+# Broken heading
```

## Links

A link in a document leads somewhere that exists.

| id | title | check | fix | requirement |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`markdown/links`](#relative-links-and-anchors-resolve) | Relative links and anchors resolve | warn · command |  |  |

### Relative links and anchors resolve

`markdown/links` · file · warn · command · markdown

*A link to a file or a heading that has moved is dead on arrival, and nothing but a check finds it. The check is lychee, offline: it reads the links of a document and opens only the files they name, with their fragments, and makes no request. A link to another site is outside the decision. Lychee is chosen over a check of our own on the document tree. The tree names every link, but a link is a subject only once the Markdown provider states sections and links as subjects (MD2); until then a CEL check sees a file's text and facts, not its nodes, and would have to parse Markdown a second time. Lychee already resolves relative paths against the file, reads fragments the way GitHub slugs headings, and is the tool the documentation world uses. When MD2 gives links, a CEL check over them replaces the program and this reasoning with it. The program is not bundled. A project without lychee on its `PATH` has an incomplete analysis for its Markdown files, never a clean one. The finding of a file that fails is the end of what lychee printed, which names each broken link.*

A relative link, and the heading it points to, MUST exist.

Derived from: lychee: https://github.com/lycheeverse/lychee; GitHub Flavored Markdown spec, links: https://github.github.com/gfm/#links; markdownlint MD051 link-fragments: https://github.com/DavidAnson/markdownlint/blob/main/doc/md051.md

```markdown invalid
# Title

See [the guide](guide.md).
```

```markdown valid guide.md
# Guide
```
